summary: This wiki note collects several Royal Dutch Shell developments: the 2007 re-branding deal with Reitan Group's 7-Eleven stations in Scandinavia, the 2010 sale of Shell's Finnish and Swedish downstream assets to St1, and Shell's divestment plans in Africa and Nigeria. It also covers Niger Delta pollution disputes, the 2004-2005 creation of Royal Dutch Shell plc as a single parent company, and Shell's 2014 sale of Woodside Petroleum shares, which failed a shareholder buy-back vote.
one_line: A collection of Royal Dutch Shell's asset sales, Niger Delta pollution disputes, 2005 corporate unification, and Woodside stake sell-down.
key_facts: On 27 August 2007, Royal Dutch Shell and Reitan Group announced an agreement to re-brand some 269 service stations across Norway, Sweden, Finland and Denmark.
In October 2010, Shell's gas stations and heavy vehicle fuel supply networks in Finland and Sweden, along with a refinery in Gothenburg, Sweden, were sold to St1, a Finnish energy company.
The Finnish and Swedish stations sold to St1 were to be rebranded within a maximum of five years from the acquisition, and they would operate under Shell brand licence until then.
In April 2010, Shell announced its intention to divest from downstream business in all African countries except South Africa and Egypt, with Vitol and "Helios" named as potential buyers.
Shell continued upstream crude oil extraction in the Niger Delta and downstream activities in South Africa after its African divestment plans were announced.
In June 2013, Shell announced a strategic review of its Nigerian operations, and in August 2014 it was finalizing the sale of its interests in four Nigerian oil fields.
In January 2013, a Dutch court rejected four of five allegations against Shell over Niger Delta oil pollution but found a subsidiary guilty of one case, ordering compensation to a Nigerian farmer.
In November 2004, Shell announced a single capital structure with a new parent company, Royal Dutch Shell plc, following the revelation that Shell had overstated its oil reserves.

Royal Dutch Shell plc had its primary listing on the London Stock Exchange, a secondary listing on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, headquarters and tax residency in The Hague, and its registered office in London.
The unification was completed on 20 July 2005, and Royal Dutch Petroleum Company was delisted from the NYSE on 18 November 2005.
Shares of the unified company were issued at a 60/40 advantage for the shareholders of Royal Dutch, in line with the original ownership of the Shell Group.
In June 2014, Shell sold 9.5% of its 23.1% stake in Woodside Petroleum and agreed that Woodside would buy back 9.5% of its shares at a later stage.
Shell became a major Woodside shareholder after a 2001 takeover attempt was blocked by then federal Treasurer Peter Costello.
At a general meeting on 1 August 2014, 72 percent of Woodside shareholders voted to approve the buy-back, short of the 75 percent required.
Shell said it was reviewing its options for its remaining 13.6 percent holding in Woodside Petroleum.
